A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CUDA-L1 and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Appendices A–B and the references match apart from pagination, supporting a reliable full comparison.

before.justification: v8 reports original KernelBench evaluations, comparisons across five GPU architectures, training-component ablations, and optimization case studies.

after.justification: v10 retains the original KernelBench results, GPU transfer evaluations, ablations, and optimization case studies.

M1.justification: The three-stage training pipeline, contrastive prompts, exemplar sampling, rewards, and GRPO objective remain unchanged. The added lazy-output safeguards concern evaluation validation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 250 KernelBench tasks and evaluate across A100, H100, L40, RTX 3090, and H20. The new illustrative lazy-matmul code does not establish additional evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same PyTorch, Torch Compile, Reduce Overhead, and CUDA Graph comparisons, together with the same vanilla and evolutionary LLM comparators and CUDA-L1 variants.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 extends the stated validation procedure with output type, device, allocated-storage, and pointer checks intended to prevent deferred computation from escaping timing. Existing timing budgets and metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish benchmark reruns.

E4.justification: v10 adds a qualitative lazy-evaluation failure case with illustrative exploit and validation code in Section 3.1. Existing training-stage, sampling, LSTM, and Conv3d ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated timing, randomized execution order, seven-bucket variance control, verification thresholds, and best-of-five baseline reporting are retained. No new uncertainty estimates, seed information, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: The added qualitative finding is a community-detected loophole that defers computation until the correctness check. Tables 4–9 retain their numerical results, including A100 mean and median speedups of 3.12 and 1.42; no measured effect of the new safeguards is reported.

T1.justification: Definitions, sampling and reward equations, the GRPO objective, and case-study complexity arguments remain unchanged. The lazy-evaluation addition introduces no formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about contrastive RL, optimization performance, GPU portability, and discovery and combination of optimization techniques.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds a specific qualification to evaluation validity: passing numerical correctness checks does not ensure computation occurred inside the measured interval. This expands the existing discussion of timing, hyperparameter, and caching exploits.

D1.justification: v10 supplies a LazyMatmul example and concrete validation code checking tensor type, device, storage allocation, and storage pointer. Other implementation disclosures, access information, and appendix code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work inventory and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Section 2.4.3 replaces a placeholder with reference [21], which was already present and cited in v8.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the lazy-evaluation passage, correction of the citation placeholder, and an ICLR 2026 acceptance footnote. The section organization and surrounding narrative remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: Two code listings are added, and existing content reflows: Table 6 occupies a separate page, and the final conclusion sentence spills onto another page. Existing figures, table contents, and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added failure case and inspectable validation code make the reward-hacking discussion more complete and useful. The gain is limited: benchmark evidence and appendices are unchanged, and v10 provides no quantitative validation establishing that the safeguards eliminate the loophole or protect the reported results.
